In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have demonstrated that SIV lentiviruses encoding hgc can improve XSCID in the canine model, but that further work is necessary to determine if the same vector is safe and effective in the human disease.
the use of a SIN lentiviral vector encoding hgc with a RD114/TR pseudotype is safe and efficient for in vivo gene transfer and reconstitution of the immune system of XSCID dogs.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new canine model for XSCID and have successfully treated it using a lentiviral vector.
we have shown that it is feasible to correct a dog with XSCID using RD114 pseudotyping of a gammaretrovirus and have now shown it is also feasible to use a RD114 pseudotype of a SIV lentivirus.
we have developed a novel lentivector for gene therapy that can correct the immune defect in XSCID.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of SIN lentivectors pseudotyped with RD114 envelope can improve the efficacy of gene therapy for XSCIDs in dogs and possibly also in children with XSCID.
the SIV hgc vector can be used in the dog model to test safety of lentivectors and to determine whether lentiviral vectors can improve the outcome of XSCID patients.
we have developed a safe and effective lentivector system that can be used for in vivo gene delivery to HSC.
